=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Where the Seller's package departs from the Buyer's position, and recommended pushback

## 1. Headline view

The Seller's covering note describes the package as "fair and balanced". It is not. Read against the Disclosure Letter, the Seller Update does three things that work against us:

1. **It shrinks our recourse** – one low cap, one short time limit and one set of exclusions applied to *every* claim, including title, tax, fraud and the specific indemnities, combined with blanket data-room disclosure and a constructive-knowledge bar.
2. **It shifts known, quantifiable liabilities onto the Buyer after a "debt-free/cash-free" price** – Riverlark (AUD 3.2m), closing bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs), Ironquay (AUD 180k plus IP title risk) and the Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) are all pushed to or past Completion without a price or funds-flow consequence.
3. **It mischaracterises open items as closed** – the Update says Bluefen and Riverlark are "addressed" and Ironquay is "adequate", while the Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms none of these is actually done.

The inconsistency between the Update and the Disclosure Letter is itself significant: the Disclosure Letter (the document the Seller will rely on against warranty claims) is accurate about what *hasn't* happened; the Update (the document meant to persuade us) is not. We should negotiate off the Disclosure Letter's facts.

---

## 2. Liability architecture (Clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5)

### 2.1 Fundamental/title warranties folded into the general regime
**Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity".
**Why it matters:** Title is the thing we are paying AUD 24m for. If we discover a defect in title in month 19, or a loss above AUD 4.8m, we would have no recourse. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason; this is a substantive transfer of risk.
**Push back:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, share capital) capped at **100% of the purchase price**, claim period the longer of **6–7 years** or the statutory limitation period, no de minimis/basket.

### 2.2 "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"
**Why it matters:** This reverses the normal drafting default. Every protection we negotiate (tax indemnity, specific indemnities, fraud carve-out) would be silently caught unless we remember to expressly exclude it in every place. It is a trap for drafting errors.
**Push back:** Delete. Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated. Insert an express carve-out clause listing what the limitations do **not** apply to (see 2.5).

### 2.3 General cap – 20% (AUD 4.8m)
**Assessment:** 20% is at the low end for an Australian mid-market private sale where the Seller is not offering W&I insurance and where DD has surfaced a cluster of live issues (customer consent, data incident, IP title, undisclosed Completion liabilities). The known-issue profile justifies more, not less, protection.
**Push back:** Target **30–50%** for general warranties; if the Seller holds at 20–25%, the trade is a robust suite of **specific indemnities outside the cap** (see Section 3) and consider a **retention/escrow** (e.g. 10% for 18–24 months). Alternatively put W&I in play, but note the known issues will be excluded from cover, so the specific indemnities are needed regardless.

### 2.4 Thresholds and time limits
- **De minimis AUD 25,000:** acceptable in principle (≈0.1% of price), but ensure related/series claims aggregate so a single issue cannot be fragmented below the threshold.
- **Basket AUD 250,000 as a deductible** ("only the excess … is recoverable"): push for a **tipping basket** (once exceeded, recover from the first dollar). If a deductible is the landing point, hold it at or below 1% and ensure specific indemnities, tax and fundamentals are outside it.
- **18 months general:** push to **24 months** (allows one full audit cycle post-Completion plus time to investigate).
- **Tax:** separate limit – **7 years** (or 4 years from the last ATO amendment period, whichever is longer). The Seller's "tax and IP are settled under the general regime" line is a rejection of a separate tax regime; we should not accept it.
- **IP:** given Ironquay, IP warranties should carry a longer period (minimum 3 years) and a higher cap, or be backed by the Ironquay specific indemnity.

### 2.5 Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature"
**Why it matters:** As drafted this would cap and time-bar claims for fraud, breach of pre-Completion covenants, leakage/Completion adjustment disputes, the tax indemnity and every specific indemnity. An exclusive-remedy clause would also attempt to displace rescission for fraud and statutory remedies.
**Legal note:** Liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law (s 18 / s 236) cannot be contractually excluded, so the non-reliance clause is of limited effect on that front – but we should not leave the drafting in place because it will still be deployed against us on every other claim type.
**Push back:** Express carve-out so that the caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions do **not** apply to: (a) fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller or its officers; (b) fundamental warranties; (c) tax warranties and the tax indemnity; (d) each specific indemnity; (e) Completion adjustment/leakage claims; (f) breach of Seller covenants (conduct of business, restraints, confidentiality). Non-reliance to be mutual, limited to statements outside the SPA/Disclosure Letter, and expressly subject to statutory non-excludable rights.

### 2.6 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge bar
**Seller position:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
**Why it matters:** This is a **constructive knowledge** bar. Combined with general disclosure (Section 2.7), it means anything buried anywhere in the data room, or available on any public register, defeats a warranty claim – regardless of whether anyone actually understood its significance. It makes the warranties largely illusory.
**Push back:** Delete. If the Seller insists on some knowledge qualifier, limit it to **actual knowledge** of a small number of named Buyer deal-team individuals of a **specific matter fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter, and expressly exclude constructive or imputed knowledge and knowledge of advisers. Our preferred position is that disclosure (properly made) is the only knowledge-based defence.

### 2.7 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
**Seller position:** "Every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to" in the data room as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
**Why it matters:**
- "Contained *or referred to*" sweeps in documents not actually in the data room.
- No fairness standard – a single line in a 200-page contract would disclose against a warranty.
- "Publicly searchable corporate records" is open-ended (which registers? as at when? court lists? PPSR? land titles?).
- The 22 September cut-off is ~6 weeks old; anything added to the data room since is outside this disclosure but will probably be asserted as disclosed anyway.
**Push back:**
- Disclosure must be **fair disclosure**: "disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect".
- General disclosure limited to the **contents** of the data room on a **sealed index/USB** as at an agreed date (ideally the signing date, with a Buyer right to review any additions).
- Public records limited to specified searches (ASIC company extract, PPSR against the Company, relevant court registries) **as at a named date**, and only to the extent the content of the search result is itself fairly disclosed.
- Specific disclosures override general disclosure; general disclosure does not qualify fundamental or tax warranties or any specific indemnity.
- Para 1.4 (non-admission) is standard and can stay, but add that nothing in the Disclosure Letter limits the specific indemnities.

---

## 3. Known issues being shifted onto the Buyer

### 3.1 Bluefen – ~AUD 3.6m revenue (~30%) and change-of-control consent (Clause 3 / 6.3)
**Seller position:** "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent.
**Disclosure Letter says:** No final written consent and no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
**Why it matters:** Loss of Bluefen would remove ~30% of revenue. A counterparty with a change-of-control right and conditions attached has leverage to renegotiate pricing or terms around Completion. "Written consent" alone is not enough if the 11.3 conditions remain unsatisfied – the consent could lapse or be conditional.
**Push back:**
- Condition precedent to Completion: **unconditional written consent in Buyer-approved form**, confirming the 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived, and confirming no amendment to pricing, term or exclusivity as a result.
- Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours** (not "reasonable endeavours"); Buyer to be consulted on and entitled to attend communications with Bluefen; no concession to Bluefen without Buyer consent.
- Condition waivable by the **Buyer only**; appropriate long-stop date.
- Warranty that no notice of termination, non-renewal or intention to renegotiate has been received, repeated at Completion.
- Commercial fallback if the Seller cannot deliver: price reduction or deferred/contingent consideration tied to Bluefen retention for 12 months post-Completion.

### 3.2 Riverlark Bank – AUD 3.2m facility (Clause 2 / 7)
**Seller position:** Release to be provided "following Completion".
**Why it matters:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. Accepting a post-Completion release means we pay AUD 24m on an unencumbered basis and then own a company carrying AUD 3.2m of secured debt with a change-of-control trigger (clause 8.1) that may put the facility into default the moment we complete. There is no reason to accept this; it is the single clearest value transfer in the package.
**Push back:**
- Repayment **at Completion** out of the purchase price via the funds flow, against a **payout letter** from Riverlark and an executed **deed of release and discharge** of all security (including PPSR discharge and any real property mortgage), delivered as a Completion deliverable (held in escrow and released simultaneously with funds).
- Alternatively (if facility stays for any reason) a dollar-for-dollar price reduction plus Riverlark's written consent to the change of control – but this is a second-best outcome.
- Debt definition to expressly include Riverlark principal, accrued interest, break costs and fees.
- Seller indemnity for any amount payable to Riverlark not reflected in the funds flow.

### 3.3 DD-005 closing bonuses – AUD 420,000 (Funds flow)
**Seller position:** "A matter for the Seller", not itemised.
**Why it matters:** The bonuses are payable by the **Company** on Completion and continued employment. If they are not in the funds flow and not treated as Debt or transaction costs, the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) pays them. Add on-costs – superannuation (12% from 1 July 2025) and NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) – and the gross exposure is around **AUD 490,000–500,000**, not AUD 420,000. The Disclosure Letter is silent on on-costs, which should be read as "not provided for".
**Push back:**
- Treat bonuses **and all associated on-costs** (super, payroll tax, workers' comp, leave accruals if affected) as Debt / Seller Transaction Costs deducted from the price, or paid by the Seller from proceeds through the funds flow with a specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- Because payment is conditional on continued employment, agree the mechanism for amounts that become payable post-Completion (e.g. retention from price, released to Seller for any bonus that lapses).
- Confirm no other transaction-related or change-of-control payments (board, management, advisers) exist – warranty and specific indemnity.

### 3.4 Ironquay Development Studio – SOW3 IP (Clause 11.1)
**Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k) and "considered adequate".
**Why it matters:** The issue is not AUD 180k; it is that under clause 7.3 of DD-004, **title to the SOW3 Project Materials does not pass until every SOW3 fee is paid in cleared funds**. Until then the Company does not own the deliverables. If those materials are embedded in the Company's product, the value at risk is the business, not the invoice. The Disclosure Letter candidly notes there is no receipt of payment and no confirmatory assignment in the data room.
**Push back:**
- Condition precedent / Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and an executed **confirmatory IP assignment** from Ironquay (including moral rights consents from Ironquay personnel, waiver of any lien).
- Specific indemnity for **all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or be entitled to use the SOW3 Project Materials** (including re-development, licensing, third-party claims) – uncapped or capped at price, outside the basket and general time limit.
- Unqualified IP ownership warranty, not qualified by general data-room disclosure.
- Confirm no similar unpaid-fee title conditions exist in other contractor/developer agreements.

### 3.5 DD-006 data export/privacy incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6)
**Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
**Disclosure Letter says:** ~1,240 records of personal information sent to an unintended external address; investigation preliminary; unknown whether accessed, scope or whether notification required.
**Why it matters:** This is potentially an eligible data breach under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988). The assessment window is 30 days from when the entity suspected a breach; the incident predates 22 September, so the window is already closed. Post-2022 penalty regime (up to the greater of AUD 50m, 3× benefit, or 30% of turnover), the OAIC's expanded enforcement powers, and the statutory tort for serious invasion of privacy (live since June 2025) all mean the exposure is not "operational". Customer-contract consequences (Bluefen and others may have breach-notification and security obligations) also need checking. The Seller's statement that it is "not expected to be material" is a conclusion with no stated basis and is contradicted by its own disclosure that the facts are unknown.
**Push back:**
- Seller to complete the investigation pre-Completion and deliver a written report (forensic findings, access logs/recall confirmation, legal advice on notifiability, any notifications made).
- If notifiable, OAIC and individual notifications completed pre-Completion, or a Buyer-approved plan.
- **Specific indemnity**, outside the general cap and time limit (or with its own cap at price), for all loss from the incident: regulator investigation and penalties, notification and remediation costs, third-party/customer claims, and any contractual consequences under customer agreements.
- Warranties on privacy compliance, security practices and absence of other incidents, not qualified by DD-006 disclosure beyond the specific facts stated.
- Conduct-of-business covenant requiring Buyer consultation on all regulator/customer communications on the matter.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals – 3 × AUD 110,000 (DD-008 / DD-011)
**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
**Why it matters:** The Disclosure Letter's own instruction to "read together for timing/scope" and its refusal to say whether they are "unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course" suggests three related commitments that together (AUD 330k) may exceed an approval or materiality threshold that AUD 110k individually does not. Questions: Were they committed before or after the locked-box/Accounts date? Are they genuinely renewals or new scope? Are they accrued in working capital? Can they be terminated?
**Push back:**
- Confirmatory DD requests: copies of all three agreements, dates signed, approval trail, termination rights, whether reflected in the FY26 budget and Completion Accounts.
- If committed outside the ordinary course or after the relevant date, treat as **Leakage** / adjust in Completion Accounts.
- Conduct-of-business covenant: Buyer consent for any commitment >AUD 50,000 (and aggregated related commitments) between signing and Completion.
- Warranty that no supplier commitments have been split to avoid approval thresholds.

### 3.7 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
Lower risk but not closed. **Lease:** confirm the notification has been given (or is a Completion deliverable) and verify ourselves that the clause is notification-only and not a disguised consent/landlord termination right. **Mossvale:** the Seller is right that an assignment restriction is not a change-of-control clause, but we should read the full agreement ourselves (including any "deemed assignment" or control definitions) rather than rely on the Seller's characterisation. Both to be covered by a warranty that no consent, notice or approval is required under any Material Contract other than as listed in a schedule.

### 3.8 Title (DD-012)
The Seller's evidence of title is the Company's own share register, and the Disclosure Letter expressly notes we have not verified it. We should: obtain a current ASIC extract and reconcile; review the constitution for pre-emptive rights or transfer restrictions; obtain share certificates (or confirmation none issued); PPSR search against the Seller and the Company for security over the shares; confirm no options, convertibles, SAFEs, employee equity or shareholder agreements. Fundamental title warranties on the basis described in 2.1.

---

## 4. Funds flow and price mechanics
The funds flow currently omits Riverlark (AUD 3.2m), bonuses (~AUD 0.5m gross), Ironquay (AUD 0.18m) and provides no treatment for the Sandbar commitments. That is approximately **AUD 3.9m of value leakage** against a headline "debt-free/cash-free" price of AUD 24m – over 16% of the price. Require a revised, itemised funds flow showing all payments made from proceeds at Completion, and a Debt/Transaction Costs definition that expressly captures each item above.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fundamental/title warranties | Same cap/time as general | 100% of price; 6–7 yrs/statutory; no thresholds |
| 2 | "All limitations apply to all Claims" | Default-on | Delete; express carve-out list (fraud, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, leakage, covenants) |
| 3 | General cap | 20% (AUD 4.8m) | Target 30–50%; otherwise trade for uncapped specific indemnities + escrow/retention |
| 4 | Basket | Deductible AUD 250k | Tipping basket; aggregate related claims under de minimis |
| 5 | General time limit | 18 months | 24 months |
| 6 | Tax/IP | "General regime" | Separate tax warranties + tax indemnity, 7 yrs, price cap; IP ≥3 yrs backed by Ironquay indemnity |
| 7 | Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 | Apply to all Claims | Carve-outs as per #2; non-reliance mutual and subject to non-excludable statutory rights |
| 8 | Cl 8.3 Buyer knowledge | Constructive knowledge incl. data room/public records | Delete; at most actual knowledge of named individuals of fairly disclosed specific matters |
| 9 | Disclosure | Whole data room "contained or referred to" + public records | Fair-disclosure standard; sealed index at agreed date; specified searches only; no qualification of fundamentals/tax/indemnities |
| 10 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours | CP: unconditional consent in agreed form with 11.3 satisfied; all reasonable endeavours; Buyer-only waiver; fallback price/deferred consideration |
| 11 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Release post-Completion | Repay at Completion from proceeds; payout letter + deed of release + PPSR discharge as Completion deliverables |
| 12 | Bonuses AUD 420k | Not in funds flow | Treat as Debt/Transaction Costs incl. super and payroll tax (~AUD 490–500k); indemnity; retention for conditional amounts |
| 13 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to AUD 180k | Pay + confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; specific indemnity for IP title failure, outside cap |
| 14 | DD-006 privacy incident | "Not material" | Complete investigation/notifications pre-Completion; specific indemnity outside cap; unqualified privacy warranties |
| 15 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Ordinary course | Confirmatory DD; leakage/Completion Accounts treatment if outside ordinary course; conduct covenant with aggregation |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only / no consent | Verify ourselves; schedule of required consents + warranty |
| 17 | Title | Share register only | ASIC/PPSR/constitution verification; fundamental warranties |
| 18 | Funds flow | Omits ~AUD 3.9m of items | Itemised revised funds flow; expanded Debt definition |

## 6. Suggested negotiating posture
Lead with the three "known liability" items (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay) – they are quantified, uncontroversial under a debt-free/cash-free deal, and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter supports our position. Use the Seller's inconsistency between the Update and the Disclosure Letter to reframe the liability package: a Seller that cannot yet deliver Bluefen consent, a Riverlark release, Ironquay title or a concluded privacy investigation is not in a position to ask for a 20% cap, 18 months, constructive-knowledge bar and blanket disclosure. Specific indemnities for Bluefen, Ironquay and DD-006, and an escrow, are the reasonable price of the Seller's own unfinished homework.

*This note is intended to support the deal team and external counsel; it is based solely on the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter and should be checked against the full SPA draft and underlying data-room documents (DD-002 to DD-012).*

- **Basket AUD 250,000 as a deductible** ("only the excess … is recoverable"): push for a **tipping basket** (once exceeded, recover from the first dollar). If a deductible is the landing point, hold it at or below 1% and ensure specific indemnities, tax and fundamentals are outside it.
- **18 months general:** push to **24 months** (allows one full audit cycle post-Completion plus time to investigate).
- **Tax:** separate limit – **7 years** (or 4 years from the last ATO amendment period, whichever is longer). The Seller's "tax and IP are settled under the general regime" line is a rejection of a separate tax regime; we should not accept it.
- **IP:** given Ironquay, IP warranties should carry a longer period (minimum 3 years) and a higher cap, or be backed by the Ironquay specific indemnity.

### 2.5 Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature"
**Why it matters:** As drafted this would cap and time-bar claims for fraud, breach of pre-Completion covenants, leakage/Completion adjustment disputes, the tax indemnity and every specific indemnity. An exclusive-remedy clause would also attempt to displace rescission for fraud and statutory remedies.
**Legal note:** Liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law (s 18 / s 236) cannot be contractually excluded, so the non-reliance clause is of limited effect on that front – but we should not leave the drafting in place because it will still be deployed against us on every other claim type.
**Push back:** Express carve-out so that the caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions do **not** apply to: (a) fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller or its officers; (b) fundamental warranties; (c) tax warranties and the tax indemnity; (d) each specific indemnity; (e) Completion adjustment/leakage claims; (f) breach of Seller covenants (conduct of business, restraints, confidentiality). Non-reliance to be mutual, limited to statements outside the SPA/Disclosure Letter, and expressly subject to statutory non-excludable rights.

### 2.6 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge bar
**Seller position:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
**Why it matters:** This is a **constructive knowledge** bar. Combined with general disclosure (Section 2.7), it means anything buried anywhere in the data room, or available on any public register, defeats a warranty claim – regardless of whether anyone actually understood its significance. It makes the warranties largely illusory.
**Push back:** Delete. If the Seller insists on some knowledge qualifier, limit it to **actual knowledge** of a small number of named Buyer deal-team individuals of a **specific matter fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter, and expressly exclude constructive or imputed knowledge and knowledge of advisers. Our preferred position is that disclosure (properly made) is the only knowledge-based defence.

### 2.7 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
**Seller position:** "Every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to" in the data room as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
**Why it matters:**
- "Contained *or referred to*" sweeps in documents not actually in the data room.
- No fairness standard – a single line in a 200-page contract would disclose against a warranty.
- "Publicly searchable corporate records" is open-ended (which registers? as at when? court lists? PPSR? land titles?).
- The 22 September cut-off is ~6 weeks old; anything added to the data room since is outside this disclosure but will probably be asserted as disclosed anyway.
**Push back:**
- Disclosure must be **fair disclosure**: "disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect".
- General disclosure limited to the **contents** of the data room on a **sealed index/USB** as at an agreed date (ideally the signing date, with a Buyer right to review any additions).
- Public records limited to specified searches (ASIC company extract, PPSR against the Company, relevant court registries) **as at a named date**, and only to the extent the content of the search result is itself fairly disclosed.
- Specific disclosures override general disclosure; general disclosure does not qualify fundamental or tax warranties or any specific indemnity.
- Para 1.4 (non-admission) is standard and can stay, but add that nothing in the Disclosure Letter limits the specific indemnities.

## 3. Known issues being shifted onto the Buyer

### 3.1 Bluefen – ~AUD 3.6m revenue (~30%) and change-of-control consent (Clause 3 / 6.3)
**Seller position:** "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent.
**Disclosure Letter says:** No final written consent and no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
**Why it matters:** Loss of Bluefen would remove ~30% of revenue. A counterparty with a change-of-control right and conditions attached has leverage to renegotiate pricing or terms around Completion. "Written consent" alone is not enough if the 11.3 conditions remain unsatisfied – the consent could lapse or be conditional.
**Push back:**
- Condition precedent to Completion: **unconditional written consent in Buyer-approved form**, confirming the 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived, and confirming no amendment to pricing, term or exclusivity as a result.
- Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours** (not "reasonable endeavours"); Buyer to be consulted on and entitled to attend communications with Bluefen; no concession to Bluefen without Buyer consent.
- Condition waivable by the **Buyer only**; appropriate long-stop date.
- Warranty that no notice of termination, non-renewal or intention to renegotiate has been received, repeated at Completion.
- Commercial fallback if the Seller cannot deliver: price reduction or deferred/contingent consideration tied to Bluefen retention for 12 months post-Completion.

### 3.2 Riverlark Bank – AUD 3.2m facility (Clause 2 / 7)
**Seller position:** Release to be provided "following Completion".
**Why it matters:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. Accepting a post-Completion release means we pay AUD 24m on an unencumbered basis and then own a company carrying AUD 3.2m of secured debt with a change-of-control trigger (clause 8.1) that may put the facility into default the moment we complete. There is no reason to accept this; it is the single clearest value transfer in the package.
**Push back:**
- Repayment **at Completion** out of the purchase price via the funds flow, against a **payout letter** from Riverlark and an executed **deed of release and discharge** of all security (including PPSR discharge and any real property mortgage), delivered as a Completion deliverable (held in escrow and released simultaneously with funds).
- Alternatively (if facility stays for any reason) a dollar-for-dollar price reduction plus Riverlark's written consent to the change of control – but this is a second-best outcome.
- Debt definition to expressly include Riverlark principal, accrued interest, break costs and fees.
- Seller indemnity for any amount payable to Riverlark not reflected in the funds flow.

### 3.3 DD-005 closing bonuses – AUD 420,000 (Funds flow)
**Seller position:** "A matter for the Seller", not itemised.
**Why it matters:** The bonuses are payable by the **Company** on Completion and continued employment. If they are not in the funds flow and not treated as Debt or transaction costs, the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) pays them. Add on-costs – superannuation (12% from 1 July 2025) and NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) – and the gross exposure is around **AUD 490,000–500,000**, not AUD 420,000. The Disclosure Letter is silent on on-costs, which should be read as "not provided for".
**Push back:**
- Treat bonuses **and all associated on-costs** (super, payroll tax, workers' comp, leave accruals if affected) as Debt / Seller Transaction Costs deducted from the price, or paid by the Seller from proceeds through the funds flow with a specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- Because payment is conditional on continued employment, agree the mechanism for amounts that become payable post-Completion (e.g. retention from price, released to Seller for any bonus that lapses).
- Confirm no other transaction-related or change-of-control payments (board, management, advisers) exist – warranty and specific indemnity.

### 3.4 Ironquay Development Studio – SOW3 IP (Clause 11.1)
**Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k) and "considered adequate".
**Why it matters:** The issue is not AUD 180k; it is that under clause 7.3 of DD-004, **title to the SOW3 Project Materials does not pass until every SOW3 fee is paid in cleared funds**. Until then the Company does not own the deliverables. If those materials are embedded in the Company's product, the value at risk is the business, not the invoice. The Disclosure Letter candidly notes there is no receipt of payment and no confirmatory assignment in the data room.
**Push back:**
- Condition precedent / Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and an executed **confirmatory IP assignment** from Ironquay (including moral rights consents from Ironquay personnel, waiver of any lien).
- Specific indemnity for **all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or be entitled to use the SOW3 Project Materials** (including re-development, licensing, third-party claims) – uncapped or capped at price, outside the basket and general time limit.
- Unqualified IP ownership warranty, not qualified by general data-room disclosure.
- Confirm no similar unpaid-fee title conditions exist in other contractor/developer agreements.

### 3.5 DD-006 data export/privacy incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6)
**Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
**Disclosure Letter says:** ~1,240 records of personal information sent to an unintended external address; investigation preliminary; unknown whether accessed, scope or whether notification required.
**Why it matters:** This is potentially an eligible data breach under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988). The assessment window is 30 days from when the entity suspected a breach; the incident predates 22 September, so the window is already closed. Post-2022 penalty regime (up to the greater of AUD 50m, 3× benefit, or 30% of turnover), the OAIC's expanded enforcement powers, and the statutory tort for serious invasion of privacy (live since June 2025) all mean the exposure is not "operational". Customer-contract consequences (Bluefen and others may have breach-notification and security obligations) also need checking. The Seller's statement that it is "not expected to be material" is a conclusion with no stated basis and is contradicted by its own disclosure that the facts are unknown.
**Push back:**
- Seller to complete the investigation pre-Completion and deliver a written report (forensic findings, access logs/recall confirmation, legal advice on notifiability, any notifications made).
- If notifiable, OAIC and individual notifications completed pre-Completion, or a Buyer-approved plan.
- **Specific indemnity**, outside the general cap and time limit (or with its own cap at price), for all loss from the incident: regulator investigation and penalties, notification and remediation costs, third-party/customer claims, and any contractual consequences under customer agreements.
- Warranties on privacy compliance, security practices and absence of other incidents, not qualified by DD-006 disclosure beyond the specific facts stated.
- Conduct-of-business covenant requiring Buyer consultation on all regulator/customer communications on the matter.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals – 3 × AUD 110,000 (DD-008 / DD-011)
**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
**Why it matters:** The Disclosure Letter's own instruction to "read together for timing/scope" and its refusal to say whether they are "unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course" suggests three related commitments that together (AUD 330k) may exceed an approval or materiality threshold that AUD 110k individually does not. Questions: Were they committed before or after the locked-box/Accounts date? Are they genuinely renewals or new scope? Are they accrued in working capital? Can they be terminated?
**Push back:**
- Confirmatory DD requests: copies of all three agreements, dates signed, approval trail, termination rights, whether reflected in the FY26 budget and Completion Accounts.
- If committed outside the ordinary course or after the relevant date, treat as **Leakage** / adjust in Completion Accounts.
- Conduct-of-business covenant: Buyer consent for any commitment >AUD 50,000 (and aggregated related commitments) between signing and Completion.
- Warranty that no supplier commitments have been split to avoid approval thresholds.

### 3.7 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
Lower risk but not closed. **Lease:** confirm the notification has been given (or is a Completion deliverable) and verify ourselves that the clause is notification-only and not a disguised consent/landlord termination right. **Mossvale:** the Seller is right that an assignment restriction is not a change-of-control clause, but we should read the full agreement ourselves (including any "deemed assignment" or control definitions) rather than rely on the Seller's characterisation. Both to be covered by a warranty that no consent, notice or approval is required under any Material Contract other than as listed in a schedule.

### 3.8 Title (DD-012)
The Seller's evidence of title is the Company's own share register, and the Disclosure Letter expressly notes we have not verified it. We should: obtain a current ASIC extract and reconcile; review the constitution for pre-emptive rights or transfer restrictions; obtain share certificates (or confirmation none issued); PPSR search against the Seller and the Company for security over the shares; confirm no options, convertibles, SAFEs, employee equity or shareholder agreements. Fundamental title warranties on the basis described in 2.1.

## 4. Funds flow and price mechanics
The funds flow currently omits Riverlark (AUD 3.2m), bonuses (~AUD 0.5m gross), Ironquay (AUD 0.18m) and provides no treatment for the Sandbar commitments. That is approximately **AUD 3.9m of value leakage** against a headline "debt-free/cash-free" price of AUD 24m – over 16% of the price. Require a revised, itemised funds flow showing all payments made from proceeds at Completion, and a Debt/Transaction Costs definition that expressly captures each item above.

## 6. Suggested negotiating posture
Lead with the three "known liability" items (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay) – they are quantified, uncontroversial under a debt-free/cash-free deal, and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter supports our position. Use the Seller's inconsistency between the Update and the Disclosure Letter to reframe the liability package: a Seller that cannot yet deliver Bluefen consent, a Riverlark release, Ironquay title or a concluded privacy investigation is not in a position to ask for a 20% cap, 18 months, constructive-knowledge bar and blanket disclosure. Specific indemnities for Bluefen, Ironquay and DD-006, and an escrow, are the reasonable price of the Seller's own unfinished homework.
